nodes.content: Predict yeast growth effects of unseen mutation combinations across genetic backgrounds while distinguishing transferable epistasis from background-specific interactions.
requirements: Reduce combination-level RMSE by 10% versus background-aware additive models on unseen genetic backgrounds.
Exceed 75% accuracy identifying epistasis sign changes across backgrounds for independently measurable nonadditive effects.

nodes.content: Fit a hierarchical growth model with shared mutation-pair epistasis and background-genotype-conditioned deviations to predict held-out backgrounds and interaction sign flips.
How can sparse mutation-combination measurements separate transferable epistasis from genotype-conditioned sign reversals in unseen yeast backgrounds?
Marker-conditioned shrinkage toward shared pair effects will cut held-out-background RMSE ≥10% versus additive models and achieve >75% sign-flip accuracy.
Collect replicated single/double-mutant growth across sequenced backgrounds; fit marker-conditioned hierarchical effects, then evaluate held-out-background RMSE and independently measured sign flips.
Run leave-one-background-out validation across 12 strains, comparing RMSE with background-aware additivity and sign-flip accuracy on independently measured pair effects.
Across 12 held-out strains, normalized-growth RMSE improved 5% (0.114 versus 0.120); independent sign-flip accuracy reached 68%.
Adding basal transcriptomes to marker-conditioned effects should raise RMSE gains from 5% to ≥10% and sign-flip accuracy beyond 75%.
Profile basal RNA-seq in 12 strains; rerun leave-one-background-out validation using pathway scores, measuring RMSE and independent sign-flip accuracy.
Transcriptome-conditioned RMSE was 0.106 versus 0.120 additive (11.7% lower); independent sign-flip accuracy reached 78% across held-out strains.
After n8 passes benchmarks, blindly assay wild-type, single-, and double-mutant growth for 60 predicted sign-flipping pairs in four new backgrounds.
A blinded validation dataset containing triplicate wild-type, single-mutant, and double-mutant growth measurements for 60 pairs across four new backgrounds.
Select the transcriptome-conditioned model to analyze the blinded dataset, given 11.7% lower RMSE and 78% sign-flip accuracy.
Train pathway-informed graph networks on yeast interaction maps and strain variants to predict unseen-background pair effects and sign reversals.
Train an interaction-map graph network on 12 discovery strains; benchmark RMSE versus additivity and sign-flip accuracy on n10’s blinded dataset.
Train PathGNN on 12 discovery strains; preregister n10 predictions, then compare additive-baseline RMSE and independently measured sign-flip accuracy.
PathGNN v1 bundle: frozen graph weights, preregistered predictions for 60 pairs across four backgrounds, and blinded-benchmark evaluation scripts.
Do PathGNN’s frozen predictions outperform the transcriptome-conditioned model on blinded n10 pairs, particularly for cross-background epistasis sign reversals?
Unblind n10, audit triplicates, and compare frozen PathGNN, transcriptome, and additive predictions by RMSE and independently measured sign-flip accuracy.
On n10, PathGNN RMSE was 0.098 versus 0.116 additive and 0.105 transcriptome; sign-flip accuracy was 81% versus 76% transcriptome.
Replace the selected transcriptome model with PathGNN: blinded RMSE was 0.098 versus 0.105, and sign-flip accuracy 81% versus 76%.
Stratify n10 by pathway proximity and training-pair frequency; bootstrap RMSE and sign-flip accuracy for transcriptome-conditioned and frozen PathGNN models.
Across n10’s four unseen backgrounds, transcriptome-hierarchical RMSE improved 9.5% (<10% target); PathGNN improved 15.5%, leading both pathway strata.
The interaction map supports variant-conditioned inputs that distinguish mutation pairs and backgrounds without using held-out growth labels.
Audit n10 features for label leakage; retrain PathGNN without interaction edges or strain variants; compare n10 RMSE and sign-flip accuracy.
Audit found 18 n10-label-derived edges; removing them raised PathGNN RMSE to 0.119 and dropped sign-flip accuracy to 69%.
Use strain-constrained flux balance with discovery-only residual calibration to forecast growth and epistasis sign changes without held-out-derived interaction edges.
Can strain-specific metabolic constraints recover unseen-background growth and epistasis sign flips when residual calibration excludes all validation labels?
Strain-constrained iMM904 with discovery-only calibration will achieve n10 RMSE ≤0.104 versus 0.116 additive and >75% sign-flip accuracy.
Fit strain-constrained iMM904 using discovery-only calibration; score frozen predictions against n10 growth measurements and independently determined sign flips.
On n10, calibrated iMM904 achieved RMSE 0.102 versus 0.116 additive (12.1% lower) and 77% independent sign-flip accuracy.
Retire leakage-affected PathGNN and select calibrated iMM904: leakage-free n10 predictions meet both RMSE and sign-flip targets.
Ablating strain-specific reaction bounds from calibrated iMM904 will reduce n10 sign-flip accuracy below 75%.
Ablate strain-specific iMM904 reaction bounds, recalibrate on discovery strains only, and compare n10 sign-flip accuracy and RMSE against full iMM904.
After selecting calibrated iMM904, impose shared reaction bounds, refit discovery-only residuals, and compare n10 sign-flip accuracy and RMSE.
On n10, shared-bound iMM904 raised RMSE from 0.102 to 0.112 and lowered sign-flip accuracy from 77% to 70%.
Following n32, ablate only strain-specific transporter bounds, recalibrate on discovery strains, and compare n10 RMSE and sign-flip accuracy.
Reauditing n10 exposed a scoring bug: shared-bound sign-flip accuracy was 77%, not 70%; transporter-only ablation achieved 79%.
With shared-bound accuracy corrected from 70% to 77%, which reaction bounds, if any, actually drive sign-flip prediction?
No individual strain-specific bound class drives sign flips; ablating each should retain ≥75% accuracy, while shared bounds worsen RMSE.
Ablate enzyme-capacity and nutrient-uptake bounds separately; recalibrate on discovery strains and compare corrected n10 sign-flip accuracy and RMSE.
On n10, enzyme-capacity and nutrient-uptake ablations achieved 76%/78% sign-flip accuracy and 0.108/0.107 RMSE; shared-bound RMSE was 0.112.
Retain full iMM904 for its 0.102 RMSE; corrected ablation accuracies of 76–79% do not implicate any single bound class.
Use allele-specific protein-complex embeddings in a multitask Gaussian process to transfer pair effects and flag background-specific sign reversals.
After retaining iMM904, train a complex-embedding multitask GP on discovery strains; compare held-out-background RMSE and sign-flip accuracy against iMM904.
Use n14’s scripts with corrected scoring to compare complex-GP/iMM904 n10 RMSE and sign-flip accuracy, including bound-class/shared-bound ablations.
On n10, discovery-only complex-GP achieved RMSE 0.096 versus iMM904’s 0.102; independently scored sign-flip accuracy rose from 77% to 82%.
Following n42, preregister complex-GP predictions and assay replicated wild-type, single-, and double-mutant growth for 80 pairs across six unseen strains.
Blinded validation panel: preregistered complex-GP predictions and triplicate wild-type, single-, and double-mutant growth for 80 pairs across six unseen strains.
Retain iMM904 as fallback and benchmark complex-GP on n44 before adoption, despite n10 RMSE 0.096 and 82% sign-flip accuracy.
Train a discovery-only mixture of complex-GP and iMM904, gated by metabolic involvement and protein-complex membership, for unseen backgrounds.
On n44’s unseen strains, can a discovery-trained gate improve combination RMSE without sacrificing complex-GP sign-flip accuracy?
Discovery-trained metabolic/complex gating will lower n44 RMSE by ≥5% versus complex-GP while retaining ≥80% independent sign-flip accuracy.
Train a discovery-only gate, freeze mixture predictions for n44, then compare against complex-GP on RMSE and independently measured sign-flip accuracy.
On n44, gated RMSE was 0.098 versus 0.104 complex-GP and 0.118 additive; independent sign-flip accuracy was 82%.
Audit n44’s per-strain RMSE against additive and iMM904 baselines and sign-flip accuracy, then preregister prospective gated-model validation.
Audit n44 by strain: compare gated, additive, and discovery-only iMM904 RMSE; bootstrap independently measured sign-flip accuracy.
n44 audit report with per-strain gated/additive/iMM904 RMSE, bootstrap sign-flip accuracy intervals, assay exclusions, and leakage checks.
Select gated model for prospective validation over complex-GP after n44 audit; retain iMM904 fallback given gated RMSE 0.098 versus 0.104.
